newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares slip as Wall St effect dwindles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares slip as Wall St effect dwindles.

text.p: European share markets slipped on Wednesday from a strong opening as the effect of Wall Street's near-record performance overnight wore off.
The dollar was on hold as the market anxiously awaited U.S. data later in the day for clues about whether the Federal Reserve would raise official interest rates.

Leading European bourses got off to a storming start after the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 179.01 points to 6,962.03 on Tuesday. This was close to the Dow's biggest ever rise in a day in points terms, although well short of a record in percentage terms.

But by midday London had almost fallen back to Tuesday's close. German shares remained most faithful to the Wall Street lead but even they were well down from the morning high as investors became wary of Wall Street volatility.
London stocks started the day enthusiastically, with the FTSE 100 index bursting through its intra-day record of 4,466.3, set on March 11, in pre-market trading.

But dealers ruled out any spectacular performance the day before British parliamentary elections which are expected to produce a Labour government, a great unknown as the party has been in opposition for 18 years.
By midday the FTSE had sunk to 4,440.2, up 7.0 points or a modest 0.16 percent compared with the Dow's 2.64 percent rise.

"People were not quite so happy to buy at that level," said a trader after the market slipped from the high. "There's the feeling too that Wall Street is very volatile at the moment and one day's big gain doesn't make a summer."
The Wall Street rally was triggered by weaker than expected wage inflation and durable goods orders on Tuesday.

The Dow rally was only just short of a 187 point one-day rise after the "Black Monday" crash of October, 1987. But in percentage terms it was modest compared with the 10 percent gain on October 21, 1987.

Tuesday's data suggested that the Federal Open Market Committee, the U.S. central bank's policy-making arm, was less likely to strike pre-emptively against inflation by raising rates when it next meets.
"We still expect a 1/4 point rate rise on May 20," one London dealer said. "But the consensus is now swaying the other way."
In Germany the DAX rose close to an all-time high due to Wall Street before slipping. By early afternoon it was still up a robust 51.52 points or 1.52 percent at 3,434.71.

French shares were also firm but restrained with the CAC-40 index up 0.76 percent. But shares in chemical and pharmaceuticals group Rhone-Poulenc SA were up 5.75 percent to 198.7 francs after the company reported a 6.5 percent rise in its first quarter net income.
Election worries also overshadowed Paris, with a poll suggesting that the centre-right coalition government would win a narrow majority over the opposition Socialists.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar marked time before a wave of U.S. statistics later in the day. Dealers were nervous after Tuesday's weak data gave the dollar a bumpy ride.
"We're not able to do very much now ahead of the data, especially after what happened yesterday," said one trader at a Japanese bank.
Wednesday's data include first quarter gross domestic product due at 1230 GMT. It is forecast to rise by 4.1 percent after a 3.8 percent increase previously.
At 1400 GMT the market will see the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) and the New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) data, both for April.
"It's a case of stronger numbers, stronger dollar more than anything else now," said Ian Amstad, economist at Bankers Trust in London.

"Yesterday's data suggests there is no real urgency to raise rates in May, although it's still a close call. The data over the remainder of the week could be strong enough to swing the balance back in favour of a Fed rate hike."
The dollar was at 1.7283 marks at midday, up from 1.7235 in late European trade on Tuesday. It was at 126.67 yen, slightly lower than 126.75 on Tuesday.
STOCKS AT 1045 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 7.0 points or 0.16 percent at 4,440.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index rose 19.74 points (0.76 percent) at 2,622.60.
Frankfurt's DAX index gained 51.52 points (1.52 percent) to 3,434.71.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7283 marks at midday against 1.7235 in late European trade on Tuesday. It was at 126.67 yen, slightly lower than 126.75 on Tuesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $340.45 an ounce after closing in London on Tuesday at $339.95. Silver was at up two cents at $4.67.
